content: The Royal Victoria Hospital, commonly referred to as The Royal or RVH, is a major healthcare facility located in Belfast, Northern Ireland. It provides over 20% of the acute care beds in the region and treats approximately 500,000 patients annually. The hospital is currently undergoing a £74 million refurbishment project, which includes significant upgrades such as an extension to the Royal Belfast Hospital for Sick Children, the addition of new wards in the main hospital, a new Accident & Emergency department, and a new maternity unit. The hospital is situated in West Belfast, just a short distance from the city center. The hospital, completed in 1906, is a landmark in the field of building engineering and is recognized as the first air-conditioned building in the world. This innovation was made possible by the Sirocco Works factory in Belfast, which played a pioneering role in the development of air conditioning technology. Dr. Frank Pantridge, widely regarded as the father of emergency medicine, served as a cardiac consultant at the Royal Victoria Hospital for over three decades. During his tenure, he developed the portable defibrillator, a groundbreaking invention that transformed emergency medical care by enabling early treatment of cardiac arrest patients by paramedics. The hospital has also been associated with notable figures in Northern Ireland's history. Carmel Hanna, a politician from the Social Democratic and Labour Party (SDLP), worked as a nurse at the hospital. Additionally, David Ervine, a politician from the Progressive Unionist Party (PUP), was admitted to the hospital on January 7, 2007, and passed away there the following day. During the period of civil unrest known as the Northern Ireland Troubles, the Royal Victoria Hospital gained international recognition for its expertise in treating gunshot wounds, particularly injuries to the knee. The high incidence of punishment shootings targeting the kneecaps during this time led to the hospital's surgeons becoming renowned for their skill in managing such complex injuries.
